samples.summary: Empty-segment rejection turns the common "no workspace configured" case into a misleading `Invalid identifier ""` error
samples.evidence: `seg()` now throws when `encoded === ''`, and `apiV1Base()`/`apiKeysUrl()` pass `config.workspace` through it. `resolveConfig` defaults `workspace` to `''` in ALL FOUR branches (packages/cli/src/config/config.ts:100, 126, 147, 164) — i.e. whenever the user is not logged in, has no `--workspace`/`WAFFLEBASE_WORKSPACE`, and no profile workspace. Previously such a run reached the server and produced its 401/404 envelope (see the comment at config.ts:102 describing exactly that `/api/v1/workspaces//documents` state, and the regression test in test/config.test.ts:99-111). Now every workspace-scoped command AND every `--dry-run` preview fails client-side with `{"error":{"code":"ERROR","message":"Invalid identifier \"\": a URL path segment cannot be empty..."}}`, which names the wrong cause (the user supplied no identifier at all) and gives no `wafflebase login` / `--workspace` hint. The rejection is intentional per docs/design/cli.md:854, but the message and generic `ERROR` code make the most common failure mode harder to diagnose than before this change.

samples.summary: `%2e` alternatives in `DOT_SEGMENT` are dead — the regex is applied to the already-encoded value, where `%` is always `%25`
samples.evidence: `const DOT_SEGMENT = /^(?:\.|%2e){1,2}$/i` is tested against `encoded = encodeURIComponent(value)` (url.ts:32-33). `encodeURIComponent` escapes `%` to `%25`, so `encoded` can never contain a literal `%2e`; the only alternatives that can ever match are `.` and `..`. The branch's own test confirms this (test/http-client-paths.test.ts, "is neutralised, not refused, when the id merely spells one out": `%2e%2e` → `%252e%252e`, accepted). Behaviour is safe today, but the guard does not do what its doc comment claims ("percent-encoding cannot smuggle a literal `..` through"), and the dead branch would silently mislead anyone who later reuses `seg()` on a pre-encoded value or reorders the encode/test steps — at which point the real check would be gone. Either test the raw `value` for the `%2e` spellings or drop them from the pattern and state that escaping handles them.

samples.summary: `seg()` can now throw from dry-run branches that sit outside the command's own try/catch, so the error path differs per command
samples.evidence: Several commands evaluate the preview path before their `try` — docs.ts:126-129 (`docs get`), docs.ts:144-147 (`rename`), docs.ts:162 (`delete`), tabs.ts:16, 49, 73, files.ts:115, 132, 150, notes.ts:101, 119, slides.ts:106, 124. `seg()` previously never threw; now a `.`/`..`/empty identifier (or empty workspace, via `printDryRun` → `apiV1Base`) throws out of the action handler instead of reaching `outputError`. In the shipped binary `runCli` (cli.ts:75-91) still envelopes it and `outputError` sets exit 1, so observable behaviour matches — but only by the last-resort catch, and the two groups of commands now report the same input error through different paths (api-keys.ts and cells.ts catch locally, these do not). Worth moving the dry-run branch inside the existing try/catch for consistency.
